documents.unit: Clark University policies (Artificial Intelligence Use Policy)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Use Policy (Rev FY26)
documents.summary: University-wide policy covering academic, research and administrative AI use. It welcomes AI, sets principles on responsibility, disclosure, privacy and equity, and standardizes a three-tier no/limited/extensive scheme while leaving course rules to faculty.
documents.stance_why: The policy 'welcomes and encourages the use of AI' but sets no single course rule: it asks for a 'three-tier system' (no use, limited use, extensive use) and says 'faculty retain discretion in setting course and research guidelines', so it delegates with tiers.

units.why: Purpose statement: it says the policy 'promotes the responsible, ethical, transparent, and secure deployment of AI', an institution-level framework stating purpose, so P56, actor all, general, informs.
units.anchor: promotes the responsible, ethical, transparent, and secure deployment of AI

units.why: Scope sentence: 'This policy applies to all faculty, staff, students, contractors, and affiliates' sets who the framework binds, so P56 (scope), actor all.
units.anchor: applies to all faculty, staff, students, contractors, and affiliates

units.why: Legal compliance requirement: 'must comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws' binds every user as a framework condition, so P56, must, neutral.
units.anchor: must comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws

units.why: Caveat that 'AI use may not be appropriate in all contexts' is a framing principle, not a rule; P56 informs, neutral.
units.anchor: AI use may not be appropriate in all contexts

units.why: Definition of AI ('Technology and software systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence') sets what the policy covers, so P61 informs.
units.anchor: Technology and software systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence

units.why: Definition of generative AI as systems producing 'text, images, multimedia content, or code' fixes scope, so P61 informs.
units.anchor: AI systems capable of producing original content

units.why: Definition of agentic AI as systems that 'plan and carry out multi-step tasks' extends scope to agents, so P61 informs (P07 would need a rule about agents, not just a definition).
units.anchor: AI systems that can independently or with human oversight plan and carry out

units.why: The university 'welcomes and encourages the use of AI', an institution-wide default of encouragement, so P02, encourage.
units.anchor: welcomes and encourages the use of AI

units.why: 'Responsibility for AI-assisted work rests solely with the individual(s) utilizing AI' places ownership of output on users, so P29, must.
units.anchor: Responsibility for AI-assisted work rests solely with the individual(s) utilizing AI

units.why: Users are 'expected to exercise sound judgment and consider the broader ethical considerations of AI use, including environmental, societal' factors; ethics and environmental costs fit P53, should.
units.anchor: consider the broader ethical considerations of AI use, including environmental, societal, and institutional factors

units.why: 'Users should openly communicate when AI is used' is a disclosure expectation, so P24, should (soft modal), permit-side.
units.anchor: Users should openly communicate when AI is used

units.why: AI use 'must be properly attributed and not misrepresent human authorship' requires attribution, so P24, must; P29 does not fit as well because the core demand is attribution.
units.anchor: its use must be properly attributed and not misrepresent human authorship

units.why: 'AI should be leveraged to expand opportunities and minimize bias' is an equity and bias principle, so P53, should (P51 is about access and cost, which this does not state).
units.anchor: AI should be leveraged to expand opportunities and minimize bias

units.why: AI use must 'respect individual privacy, and limit unnecessary collection or exposure of sensitive information', a data-protection rule, so P50, must.
units.anchor: respect individual privacy, and limit unnecessary collection or exposure of sensitive information

units.why: The university 'reserves the right to review, restrict, or discontinue any AI tools that present unacceptable risk', an institutional vetting power, so P50 (admin, informs).
units.anchor: reserves the right to review, restrict, or discontinue any AI tools that present unacceptable risk

units.why: Cognitive offloading principle: AI should 'augment—not replace—human judgment, critical thinking', which keeps the human as primary thinker, so P32, should.
units.anchor: augment—not replace—human judgment, critical thinking, creativity, and expertise

units.why: 'Users are expected to apply critical judgment and appropriate validation when using AI outputs' tells users to verify output, so P31, should.
units.anchor: apply critical judgment and appropriate validation when using AI outputs

units.why: AI is 'not a substitute for professional, medical, mental health, legal, or academic advising services'; this limit on appropriate use fits no listed type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: not a substitute for professional, medical, mental health, legal, or academic advising services
units.uncovered_note: AI is not a substitute for professional, medical, mental-health, legal or academic advising; use for personal diagnosis or support is at the user's discretion.

units.why: 'Faculty are encouraged to explore AI’s potential in their curricula' encourages instructors to use AI in courses, so P02 (default encouragement), instructor, should.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to explore AI’s potential in their curricula

units.why: 'Syllabi and assignment guidelines should be transparent about when and how AI can or cannot be used' requires an AI statement, so P09, instructor, course-start, should.
units.anchor: should be transparent about when and how AI can or cannot be used

units.why: Expectations 'should be standardized in a three-tier system across the university', naming tiers (no use, limited use, extensive use), so P05, should.
units.anchor: standardized in a three-tier system across the university

units.why: Tier definition for no use: 'AI tools are not allowed to be used in completing that assignment or at all in the course' bans AI under that tier, so P05 (tier definition), prohibit.
units.anchor: not allowed to be used in completing that assignment or at all in the course

units.why: Tier definition for limited use: AI 'may be used in a specific way for the assignment', such as brainstorming but not writing, so P05, restrict.
units.anchor: AI may be used in a specific way for the assignment

units.why: Example under limited use: 'AI may be used to brainstorm ideas for a paper but cannot be used to write the paper'; the unit-level rule is brainstorming allowed, so P15, may.
units.anchor: AI may be used to brainstorm ideas for a paper but cannot be used

units.why: Tier definition for extensive use: 'there are no restrictions on AI use for that assignment or course', so P05, permit.
units.anchor: extensive use denotes there are no restrictions on AI use for that assignment or course

units.why: Even under extensive use the policy requires 'appropriate disclosure, labeling, and attribution', so P24, must.
units.anchor: this policy must still be followed, including but not limited to appropriate disclosure

units.why: 'Where permitted, students are invited to leverage AI for creative inquiry' welcomes student use where allowed, so P02, student, may, encourage.
units.anchor: students are invited to leverage AI for creative inquiry, responsible collaboration, and academic advancement

units.why: Condition on that permission: contribution must be 'properly disclosed', so P24, must.
units.anchor: provided its contribution is properly disclosed and does not undermine learning outcomes or misrepresent authorship

units.why: 'faculty retain discretion in setting course and research guidelines' hands the decision to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: faculty retain discretion in setting course and research guidelines

units.why: 'Research activities using AI must adhere to principles of integrity, ethical authorship, and appropriate attribution' is a research rule, so P62, must.
units.anchor: Research activities using AI must adhere to principles of integrity, ethical authorship, and appropriate attribution

units.why: 'Some disciplines or instructors may choose to minimize or avoid AI use altogether. These choices are fully supported.' confirms instructor-level freedom to restrict, so P04, may.
units.anchor: Some disciplines or instructors may choose to minimize or avoid AI use altogether

units.why: 'AI-driven solutions are encouraged for admissions, finance, financial aid, employment' encourages administrative AI, outside teaching but stated policy, so P02, admin.
units.anchor: AI-driven solutions are encouraged for admissions, finance, financial aid, employment

units.why: 'All high-impact automated decisions must include human review' is a human-in-the-loop rule for administrative AI; P46 covers only grades, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: All high-impact automated decisions must include human review
units.uncovered_note: High-impact automated (administrative) decisions must include human review; AI outputs must not be the sole basis for decisions affecting individuals.

units.why: 'all such activities must strictly protect University data and individual privacy' is a data-protection rule, so P50, must.
units.anchor: all such activities must strictly protect University data and individual privacy

units.why: AI use cannot violate 'library licensed content, copyrighted materials' or community intellectual property, a copyright and licensing limit, so P52, must-not.
units.anchor: cannot be used in ways that violate other university policy, applicable laws, other contracts

units.why: 'Sensitive data may only be used with institutionally approved, contractually vetted, and security-reviewed AI tools' restricts data to vetted tools, so P50, must-not (by limitation).
units.anchor: Sensitive data may only be used with institutionally approved, contractually vetted, and security-reviewed AI tools

units.why: 'AI tools may not be used to train external models using Clark data unless explicitly authorized' limits data sharing with AI providers, so P65, must-not.
units.anchor: may not be used to train external models using Clark data unless explicitly authorized

units.why: 'Users must promptly report suspected breaches or unauthorized disclosures to Information Technology Services' is a data-incident rule, closest to P50, must.
units.anchor: Users must promptly report suspected breaches or unauthorized disclosures

units.why: 'The Provost oversees academic standards for AI use' assigns governance roles, an institution-wide framework element, so P56 (admin, informs).
units.anchor: The Provost oversees academic standards for AI use

units.why: ITS and committees 'will monitor AI technology developments, review significant initiatives', a standing review function, so P54, admin, over-time.
units.anchor: will monitor AI technology developments, review significant initiatives

units.why: Community members are responsible for 'participating in relevant training or compliance programs'; a training duty fits no type (P63 is about supporting faculty), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: participating in relevant training or compliance programs
units.uncovered_note: All community members must align AI use with the policy and take part in relevant training or compliance programs.

units.why: 'responsible for the content they provide, whether the content was created using AI or not' makes people own what they provide, so P29, must.
units.anchor: responsible for the content they provide, whether the content was created using AI or not

units.why: 'Violations of this policy may result in corrective action according to existing University procedures' routes misuse to existing processes, so P36, when-misuse.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy may result in corrective action according to existing University procedures

units.why: The policy 'operates alongside, and does not replace, other University policies governing academic integrity', a scope statement, so P56.
units.anchor: operates alongside, and does not replace, other University policies governing academic integrity

units.why: 'their use must be disclosed in a clear and appropriate manner' is the general disclosure mandate, so P24, must.
units.anchor: their use must be disclosed in a clear and appropriate manner

units.why: Academic citation must include 'a brief description of how the tool was used' and 'identification of the tool or service', specific citation details, so P25, must.
units.anchor: including a brief description of how the tool was used

units.why: In administrative contexts 'AI use must be documented when it materially influences decisions', a disclosure duty for staff, so P24, admin.
units.anchor: AI use must be documented when it materially influences decisions, analyses, recommendations

units.why: 'individuals remain responsible for the accuracy, integrity, and ethical use of AI-assisted content' restates ownership tied to accuracy, so P29.
units.anchor: individuals remain responsible for the accuracy, integrity, and ethical use

units.why: 'Next Review Date November, 2026' sets a review cycle, so P54, admin, over-time.
units.anchor: Next Review Date November, 2026

documents.title: Teach with AI
documents.summary: Faculty guidance page from Clark's AI Hub. It offers sample syllabus language for three use levels, assignment ideas, advice for students who object to AI, uses of AI in teaching, and cautions on AI detectors.
documents.stance_why: The page offers three tiers ('No use', 'Limited use', 'Extensive use') with sample syllabus text and says 'Integrating AI into your courses, or choosing not to, starts with clear communication', so it hands the choice to instructors and delegates.

units.why: Recommends 'a three-tiered framework for your assignments or your course as a whole', named tiers for instructors, so P05, should.
units.anchor: a three-tiered framework for your assignments or your course as a whole

units.why: No use tier is for foundational steps 'where the struggle is the learning', a skill-building rationale, so P41, informs.
units.anchor: foundational steps where the struggle is the learning

units.why: Limited use tier: students use AI 'for specific, restricted tasks' with final writing their own, so P05, restrict.
units.anchor: use AI behind the scenes as a helpful partner for specific, restricted tasks

units.why: Under limited use 'they must disclose where and how they used AI', so P24, must.
units.anchor: they must disclose where and how they used AI

units.why: Extensive use tier: 'few or no restrictions on how the tool is used for that assignment', so P05, permit.
units.anchor: few or no restrictions on how the tool is used for that assignment

units.why: Even at the extensive level, 'a student properly disclosing and attributing the use of AI' is still expected, so P24.
units.anchor: does not negate a student properly disclosing and attributing the use of AI

units.why: Sample No Use syllabus text: 'all work must be completed completely on your own without any assistance from generative AI tools' is a blanket ban, so P01, prohibit.
units.anchor: all work must be completed completely on your own without any assistance from generative AI

units.why: Rationale in the No Use sample: 'The only way to build those skills is to go through the cognitive struggle yourself', so P41, informs.
units.anchor: The only way to build those skills is to go through the cognitive struggle yourself

units.why: No Use sample lists permitted non-AI tools ('Standard spell-check, word processors, library databases'), clarifying the scope of the ban, so P61, informs.
units.anchor: Standard spell-check, word processors, library databases, and course readings

units.why: 'Using AI at any stage of your work—including brainstorming topics' bans all AI help including brainstorming; closest type is P19 (AI may not produce the work), though broader, chosen over P01 which is the default-ban statement already coded.
units.anchor: Using AI at any stage of your work—including brainstorming topics, organizing outlines, or drafting paragraphs

units.why: 'All submitted work must be entirely your own' is ownership of submissions, so P29, must.
units.anchor: All submitted work must be entirely your own

units.why: Limited Use sample: AI may help 'brainstorm topics, structure rough outlines', so P15, may.
units.anchor: Using AI to help you brainstorm topics, structure rough outlines

units.why: Same sentence allows AI to 'check your written grammar', a prose-specific use, so P18, may.
units.anchor: check your written grammar

units.why: Same sentence allows AI as a 'conversational study partner to quiz you on concepts', a study aid use, so P14, may.
units.anchor: act as a conversational study partner to quiz you on concepts

units.why: 'You must disclose where and how you used AI in all cases' is the Limited Use disclosure rule, so P24, must.
units.anchor: You must disclose where and how you used AI in all cases

units.why: 'Having an AI write sentences, paragraphs, or blocks of code for your final submissions' is listed as not allowed, so P19, must-not.
units.anchor: Having an AI write sentences, paragraphs, or blocks of code for your final submissions

units.why: 'The core arguments, unique perspectives, and final phrasing must come from you' keeps the student as thinker, so P32, must.
units.anchor: The core arguments, unique perspectives, and final phrasing must come from you

units.why: Extensive Use sample: 'You are encouraged to work directly alongside these tools', default encouragement for that course, so P02, encourage.
units.anchor: You are encouraged to work directly alongside these tools

units.why: Rationale: 'Learning how to effectively co-create with AI is an essential professional skill', so P44, informs.
units.anchor: Learning how to effectively co-create with AI is an essential professional skill

units.why: Grading 'will focus heavily on your human judgment' (critique, audit, fact-check), a grading redesign around AI, so P35.
units.anchor: our grading will focus heavily on your human judgment

units.why: 'Using AI to help generate drafts, write code, analyze data sets, or build project components' allows AI-generated code and drafts, so P16, may.
units.anchor: Using AI to help generate drafts, write code, analyze data sets, or build project components

units.why: 'You must clearly disclose and attribute how you used the tools for every assignment' is the extensive-use disclosure rule, so P24, must.
units.anchor: You must clearly disclose and attribute how you used the tools for every assignment

units.why: 'Your success in this class depends entirely on the human validation step' expects students to check AI output, so P31, should.
units.anchor: Your success in this class depends entirely on the human validation step

units.why: AI Peer Review idea: students 'turn in both their prompt history, and a short reflection', transcripts and reflections, so P26.
units.anchor: They turn in both their prompt history, and a short reflection explaining

units.why: Fact-checking idea gives students 'AI generated code' to audit for inefficiencies and insecure variables; assignment redesign around AI, so P35, instructor, may.
units.anchor: give students AI generated code that produces the correct output, and have them identify inefficiencies

units.why: Socratic idea: 'submit the chat transcript along with a paragraph summarizing what they learned', so P26 (transcript plus reflection).
units.anchor: submit the chat transcript along with a paragraph summarizing what they learned

units.why: Instructors can 'have students use a prompt that turns the AI into a Socratic tutor' to learn a concept, a tutor use, so P12, instructor, may.
units.anchor: Have students use a prompt that turns the AI into a Socratic tutor

units.why: 'Clark’s own Mark Jacobs has created a custom Socratic Dialog tool' points to a university-built course tool, so P17, informs.
units.anchor: Clark’s own Mark Jacobs has created a custom Socratic Dialog tool

units.why: 'Students are responsible for the work they submit, including any content created or informed by AI', so P29, must.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for the work they submit, including any content created or informed

units.why: Faculty 'should help students understand that the responsible use of AI does not replace original thinking', an instructor duty to communicate, so P32, should.
units.anchor: responsible use of AI does not replace original thinking, disciplinary knowledge, or personal accountability

units.why: AI-detection tools 'cannot reliably determine whether AI was used' and 'should not be considered definitive evidence', so P39, instructor, should-not.
units.anchor: should not be considered definitive evidence of academic misconduct

units.why: 'Suspected violations should be addressed through Clark’s existing academic integrity process' treats misuse as misconduct handled by integrity processes, so P36, should.
units.anchor: Suspected violations should be addressed through Clark’s existing academic integrity process

units.why: Opt-out path: instructors should let objecting students 'meet the exact same learning goals using traditional research methods or peer collaboration', an alternative-access rule, so P51, should.
units.anchor: meet the exact same learning goals using traditional research methods or peer collaboration instead

units.why: 'Clearly explain exactly why you are asking them to use it for this specific task' tells instructors to justify required AI use, a rationale about career skills, so P44, should.
units.anchor: Clearly explain exactly why you are asking them to use it for this specific task

units.why: Instructors may 'ask an AI to brainstorm five different real-world analogies', AI for teaching work, so P59, may.
units.anchor: ask an AI to brainstorm five different real-world analogies

units.why: Instructors can 'ask it to draft a detailed scoring rubric' and generate template feedback, a teaching-work use, so P59 (final grading would be P46).
units.anchor: ask it to draft a detailed scoring rubric based on your specific criteria

units.why: Instructors can have AI 'generate multiple-choice questions or short-answer prompts' with an answer key, quiz item drafting, so P59.
units.anchor: instruct it to generate multiple-choice questions or short-answer prompts

units.why: 'Mark partners with faculty to navigate academic integrity, design assignments, and integrate AI into courses' is faculty support, so P63.
units.anchor: Mark partners with faculty to navigate academic integrity, design assignments, and integrate AI into courses

units.why: 'This website was drafted with generative AI assistance (Gemini and Copilot)' discloses AI use in producing materials, so P48 (AI-made materials disclosed).
units.anchor: This website was drafted with generative AI assistance (Gemini and Copilot)

notes: No school or computing-unit policy found; course layer deferred in collect. Three UNCOVERED units: non-substitute for advising, human review of administrative decisions, and community training duty.
